title: Unit 05: Book-II Heroes Part 2 (Sir Alexander Fleming, Louis Pasteur)
subject: english-12

questions.question: In Patrick Pringle's biographical essay on Sir Alexander Fleming, what major flaw of chemical antiseptics (like carbolic acid) during WW1 is highlighted?

options.A: They were too expensive to manufacture in wartime.
options.B: They destroyed the body's natural defense cells (leucocytes / white blood cells) more effectively than they killed the invading bacteria.
options.C: They had an unpleasant smell that caused headaches.
options.D: They caused immediate chemical fires in field hospitals.

questions.explanation: Sir Almroth Wright and Fleming proved that chemical antiseptics did more harm than good in deep wounds by killing leucocytes while bacteria survived deep in tissues.

questions.question: What natural antibacterial enzyme did Fleming discover in human tears, saliva, and mucus in 1922?

options.A: Penicillin
options.B: Lysozyme
options.C: Streptomycin

questions.explanation: Fleming discovered Lysozyme when a drop of his nasal mucus accidentally fell on a culture plate and dissolved surrounding bacteria, demonstrating the body's natural defense.

questions.question: How did Fleming serendipitously discover Penicillin at St. Mary's Hospital in 1928?

options.A: By deliberately importing radioactive fungi from South America
options.B: A drifting mould spore (Penicillium notatum) contaminated an uncovered culture plate of Staphylococcus bacteria, creating a transparent ring of dissolved microbes
options.C: By injecting snake venom into guinea pigs

questions.explanation: A stray spore blew in through the window, settled on a staphylococcus culture plate, and Fleming noticed that bacteria surrounding the mould were being lysed and destroyed.

questions.question: Why could Fleming not immediately produce Penicillin as a clinical drug in 1928?

options.A: He was forbidden by British medical authorities.
options.B: Penicillin was extraordinarily unstable and elusive; as a bacteriologist, he lacked the biochemical team and funding to concentrate and purify it.
options.C: He lost his laboratory in a fire.
options.D: The mould refused to grow again.

questions.explanation: Purifying unstable penicillin required advanced chemical engineering, which was only achieved a decade later by Florey and Chain at Oxford.

questions.question: Which Oxford University scientists successfully isolated, purified, and mass-produced Penicillin during the crisis of World War II?

options.A: Howard Florey and Ernst Chain
options.B: Louis Pasteur and Robert Koch
options.C: James Watson and Francis Crick

questions.explanation: Sir Howard Florey and Dr. Ernst Chain headed the Oxford research team that turned Fleming's raw mould juice into the miracle wonder drug.

questions.question: Why did Sir Alexander Fleming refuse to patent his discovery of Penicillin for personal financial gain?

options.A: Because British patent law prohibited medical patents.
options.B: He believed his discovery was a gift of nature for the healing of humanity, not a commodity to amass personal wealth.
options.C: He was already the richest man in Scotland.
options.D: His university claimed all commercial royalties.

questions.explanation: Fleming displayed profound humanitarian modesty, insisting that penicillin belonged to the entire world without commercial copyright.

questions.question: In Margaret Avery's essay on Louis Pasteur, what fundamental biological theory did Pasteur definitively disprove?

options.A: The theory of Spontaneous Generation (abiogenesis)
options.B: The germ theory of disease
options.C: Mendel's laws of inheritance

questions.explanation: Pasteur used swan-necked flasks to prove that living microbes arise only from existing living germs in the air, disproving the ancient myth that life originates spontaneously from decaying matter.

questions.question: What industrial crisis in France did Pasteur solve by introducing the process that now bears his name (Pasteurization)?

options.A: The spoiling of wine and beer due to unwanted bacterial fermentation
options.B: The explosion of coal mines from methane gas
options.C: The rusting of steel railroad tracks

questions.explanation: Pasteur showed that heating wine and beer to 50–60°C killed harmful microbes without destroying the flavor, saving the French brewing and wine industries.

questions.question: What devastating disease of silkworms did Pasteur investigate, saving the French silk industry in the south of France?

options.A: Pebrine and Flacherie
options.B: Bovine tuberculosis
options.C: Rinderpest

questions.explanation: Pasteur spent years in the Cévennes region, showing silkworm breeders how to use microscopes to detect diseased moths and eradicate pebrine.

questions.question: What historic public demonstration of anthrax vaccination did Pasteur conduct at Pouilly-le-Fort in 1881?

options.A: He vaccinated 25 sheep against anthrax, left 25 unvaccinated, and injected all 50 with deadly anthrax culture; every vaccinated sheep survived while all unvaccinated died.
options.B: He drank anthrax broth in front of the French Academy of Sciences.
options.C: He injected himself with rabid wolf saliva.

questions.explanation: The Pouilly-le-Fort experiment was a sensational triumph: all 25 vaccinated sheep were perfectly healthy, while the 25 control sheep lay dead or dying.

questions.question: Who was the first human patient successfully treated by Pasteur for rabies (hydrophobia) in July 1885?

options.A: Joseph Meister, a nine-year-old Alsatian boy severely bitten by a mad dog
options.B: A French shepherd named Jean-Baptiste Jupille
options.C: His own son

questions.explanation: Little Joseph Meister had fourteen deep wounds from a rabid dog; Pasteur's series of 13 attenuated spinal cord injections prevented rabies and saved his life.

questions.question: How did Pasteur attenuate (weaken) the rabies virus in his laboratory?

options.A: By drying infected spinal cords of rabbits in sterile dry air flasks for varying numbers of days
options.B: By boiling rabies tissue in carbolic acid
options.C: By exposing the virus to X-ray radiation
options.D: By freezing it in glacier ice

questions.explanation: Drying rabid rabbit spinal cords day by day systematically weakened the virus, allowing Pasteur to build immunity through progressively stronger doses.

questions.question: What magnificent international institute was erected in Paris through global public subscription in honor of Pasteur's rabies breakthrough?

options.A: The Pasteur Institute (Institut Pasteur)
options.B: The Sorbonne Medical Center
options.C: The Fleming Foundation

questions.explanation: Gratitude from around the globe funded the Institut Pasteur in Paris, dedicated to biological research, microbiology, and vaccine development.

questions.question: What personal physical handicap did Louis Pasteur overcome during the peak of his scientific career?

options.A: He suffered a severe stroke at age 46 that left his left side permanently paralyzed, yet he continued laboratory work for decades.
options.B: He was completely blind from birth.
options.C: He lost both legs in the Franco-Prussian war.

questions.explanation: Despite being semi-paralyzed from a cerebral hemorrhage in 1868, Pasteur's iron will drove him to make his greatest discoveries in anthrax and rabies.

questions.question: What is the defining biological difference between an antiseptic and an antibiotic?

options.A: Antiseptics are non-specific toxic chemicals used on skin/instruments, whereas antibiotics are biological substances produced by organisms that destroy specific bacteria inside the body without harming host cells.
options.B: Antiseptics cure viral infections while antibiotics cure bacterial diseases.
options.C: Antibiotics are injected into wounds directly while antiseptics are swallowed as tablets.
options.D: There is no difference; they are identical synonyms.

questions.explanation: Antiseptics (e.g. iodine, phenol) destroy living tissue cells indiscriminately; antibiotics (e.g. penicillin) target microbial cell walls without killing human cells.

questions.question: In 1945, who jointly received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the discovery and development of Penicillin?

options.A: Sir Alexander Fleming, Howard Florey, and Ernst Chain
options.B: Louis Pasteur, Robert Koch, and Joseph Lister
options.C: Almroth Wright, Joseph Meister, and Patrick Pringle

questions.explanation: Fleming shared the 1945 Nobel Prize with Florey and Chain for discovering and purifying penicillin.

questions.question: What patriotic action did Pasteur take during the Franco-Prussian War of 1870?

options.A: He volunteered to fight as an infantry rifleman despite his paralysis and returned his honorary diploma to the University of Bonn in protest against Prussian aggression.
options.B: He moved to Germany to conduct research.
options.C: He designed chemical weapons for the military.

questions.explanation: Pasteur was deeply patriotic; he tried to enlist in the National Guard and returned his Prussian honorary medical degree in moral protest.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the medical term 'attenuation' in immunology?

options.A: Weakening the virulence of a pathogen so it stimulates immunity without causing disease
options.B: Multiplying bacteria in nutrient broth
options.C: Surgically amputating an infected limb

questions.explanation: 'Attenuation' is the reduction of virulence in a microbe, enabling its use as a safe, protective vaccine.

questions.question: Fleming's childhood upbringing in rural Ayrshire, Scotland, gave him what invaluable scientific trait?

options.A: Keen powers of natural observation and deep appreciation for living nature
options.B: Training in finance and stockbroking
options.C: Fluency in classical Greek

questions.explanation: Growing up on a moorland farm cultivated Fleming's sharp eyes, observational patience, and curiosity about natural phenomena.

questions.question: What was the popular moniker given to Penicillin after its miracle efficacy was demonstrated in treating WW2 battle casualties?

options.A: 'The Wonder Drug'
options.B: 'The Black Salve'
options.C: 'The Elixir of Gold'

questions.explanation: Penicillin saved countless Allied soldiers from septic gangrene and pneumonia, earning universal fame as 'The Wonder Drug'.

questions.question: What was Pasteur's answer to critics who claimed spontaneous generation occurred in boiled broth?

options.A: He showed that if air entering the flask was filtered or passed through a bent swan-neck curve, dust carrying microbes could not enter, and the broth remained sterile indefinitely.
options.B: He added poison to the broth.
options.C: He sealed the flasks inside iron boxes.
options.D: He performed his experiments at midnight.

questions.explanation: The swan-neck flask experiment proved that gravity trapped dust particles in the bend, keeping the broth perfectly clear and free of microbial life.

questions.question: What famous quote is attributed to Louis Pasteur regarding scientific observation?

options.A: 'Chance favors only the prepared mind.'
options.B: 'All discoveries are completely accidental.'
options.C: 'Science has no place for imagination.'

questions.explanation: Pasteur emphasized that serendipitous scientific accidents yield discoveries only when an observer has the trained intellect to understand them.

questions.question: What was the initial medical response when Fleming published his 1929 paper on Penicillin?

options.A: Massive global excitement and immediate commercial manufacture
options.B: Virtually complete indifference and silence, as few grasped its revolutionary therapeutic significance
options.C: He was knighted by the King the following morning
options.D: The paper was burned by medical journals

questions.explanation: The British Journal of Experimental Pathology paper attracted almost zero public interest until Florey and Chain revived it in 1939.

questions.question: What fatal disease caused by hydrophobia did Pasteur overcome with his vaccine?

options.A: Rabies
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Tetanus

questions.explanation: Rabies (hydrophobia) was 100% fatal once symptoms appeared; Pasteur's post-exposure prophylaxis was a monumental breakthrough in medical history.

questions.question: Identify the figure of speech in: 'Penicillin was a magic bullet that hunted down bacteria without injuring body tissues.'

options.A: Metaphor
options.B: Simile
options.C: Litotes

questions.explanation: Directly identifying penicillin as a 'magic bullet' without using 'like' or 'as' is an imaginative metaphor.

questions.question: What is the synonym of 'serendipity' in scientific history?

options.A: Deliberate and planned mathematical calculation
options.B: The occurrence of valuable discoveries by happy chance or fortunate accident
options.C: Severe intellectual fatigue

questions.explanation: 'Serendipity' is the fortunate discovery of something valuable while looking for something else, perfectly typified by Fleming's mould.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'Fleming was modest and objected _____ being lionized by the global press.'

options.A: at
options.B: to
options.C: against

questions.explanation: The verb 'object' requires the preposition 'to' followed by a gerund ('objected to being lionized').

questions.question: What is the meaning of 'lionized' in the sentence above?

options.A: Attacked by wild lions
options.B: Treated as a celebrated celebrity and hero with immense public adoration
options.C: Exiled to an African safari

questions.explanation: 'To lionize' someone means to shower them with immense public celebration, adulation, and celebrity status.

questions.question: In what year did Fleming discover the penicillin mould contamination on his culture plate?
questions.explanation: Fleming discovered penicillin in September 1928 at St. Mary's Hospital, London.

questions.question: How did Joseph Meister express his lifelong gratitude to Louis Pasteur?

options.A: He became the gatekeeper and caretaker of the Pasteur Institute until his death
options.B: He paid Pasteur a monthly pension
options.C: He wrote a best-selling novel about him
options.D: He named his village after Pasteur

questions.explanation: Joseph Meister served loyally as the gatekeeper of the Pasteur Institute in Paris for the rest of his life.

questions.question: What happened when Nazi officers ordered Joseph Meister to open Pasteur's crypt during the 1940 occupation of Paris?

options.A: He gladly opened the doors and guided them.
options.B: He chose suicide rather than desecrate Pasteur's resting place for the invading Germans.
options.C: He fled across the English Channel.
options.D: He surrendered the keys to the municipal mayor.

questions.explanation: In 1940, the elderly Meister chose to end his own life rather than permit Nazi soldiers to enter and violate Pasteur's sacred tomb.

questions.question: What is the antonym of 'virulent' in microbiology?

options.A: Malignant
options.B: Innocuous / Harmless / Benign
options.C: Fatal

questions.explanation: 'Virulent' means extremely severe, harmful, or deadly; its opposite is benign, harmless, or innocuous.

questions.question: Which of the following demonstrates correct use of the subjunctive mood?

options.A: It is essential that Fleming receives all the credit.
options.B: It is essential that Fleming receive all the credit.
options.C: It is essential that Fleming will receive all the credit.
options.D: It is essential that Fleming received all the credit.

questions.explanation: Subjunctive expressions ('it is essential that...') require the base form of the verb ('receive').

questions.question: What did Fleming frequently say about his role in the penicillin discovery?

options.A: 'I invented penicillin by sheer genius.'
options.B: 'Nature created penicillin; I only found it.'
options.C: 'Florey and Chain did all the work.'
options.D: 'Microbiology is a game of chance without science.'

questions.explanation: Fleming characteristically deflected praise by noting that the mould had existed for millions of years in nature, and he had merely observed its effect.

questions.question: What supreme moral quality unites Sir Alexander Fleming and Louis Pasteur?

options.A: Unflinching dedication to alleviating human disease through patient empirical science, combined with selfless humanitarian modesty
options.B: A desire for personal wealth through patent monopolies
options.C: Interest in military weaponry and politics
options.D: Refusal to train students in laboratories

questions.explanation: Both Fleming and Pasteur dedicated their lives selflessly to conquering deadly diseases for the salvation of humanity.
